newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.N. and aid workers held in Iran to be freed.
newsitem.headline: U.N. and aid workers held in Iran to be freed.

text.p: A U.N. official and three aid workers who were seized in northern Iraq and taken across the border to Iran are expected to be released later on Sunday, a United Nations official said.

United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) official in Tehran Laurens Jolles confirmed a report from the French aid group Pharmaciens sans Frontieres (PSF) in Paris that Pierre Vinet, UNHCR representative in northern Iraq, and three PSF workers were being held in Iran.
PSF said in a statement from Paris on Saturday that exiled leaders of an Iraqi Kurdish group reported the four were being held by Iranian troops. They were in good health and had not been mistreated.
They were seized on Friday near the Iran-Iraq border while visiting refugees displaced by the capture of Sulaimaniya by a rival Kurdish faction.
"They are in Iran and it seems they will be released tonight. I don't have any more details. The Iranian authorities have them," Jolles said.
Jolles told Reuters by telephone that the four, including PSF member Guillaume Woehling, an Iraqi PSF doctor and an Iraqi driver, would be handed over to the UNHCR.
